reasons: Variant compiles; the trigger TypeUtilsTest::testTypesSatisfyVariables fails at line 516 (G extends Comparable<G>, G=Integer); the full suite shows only the trigger newly failing; the three ownership tests pass. Trace: conformsTo(Integer, Comparable<G>, {G->Integer}) builds toTypeVarAssigns = {G->Integer, T->Integer} (getTypeArguments copies the given assignments, as in pristine); for key G the subject map has no entry, so fromTypeArg is null, and without the omitted null skip the gold returns false. (a) All callees of the gold (getRawType, getTypeArguments, unrollVariableAssignments) return correct values, and the gold's own contract (true if type is assignable to the parameterized type under the given assignments) is violated: Integer is assignable to Comparable<Integer>. Hops 1-4 only propagate it. (b) Each hop's javadoc matches its code. Hop 3 substitutes only a bound that is itself a type variable, as documented and as pristine substituteTypeVariables does. Hop 4 is a dispatch identical to TypeUtils.isAssignable's ParameterizedType branch and passes the assignments as documented. (c) Hop-level edits that keep the gold live all fail the trigger: dropping or replacing the map makes Comparable<G> unresolvable (an NPE in the gold), and value or type-variable guards do not reach the failing case. The only passing non-gold edits route around conformsTo (at hop 4 or hop 3) to TypeUtils.isAssignable, which makes the gold dead: bypasses. (d) Hop names are neutral; G2b-style scan is clean; the lie (copy into a sorted map, check bounds last to first) does not mention the null skip or any hop. (e) The gold is exactly five calls below the facade. The hosts are five distinct existing classes (ArrayUtils, FastDateFormat, StrBuilder, ToStringStyle, StringUtils). The facade body is a single delegating call (the original had no guard). The one added procedural sentence is not performed by the code. The gold's javadoc is silent on absent variables. test.patch is empty and the trigger is an existing test. (f) TypeUtils.isAssignable(Type, ParameterizedType, Map) keeps the explicit 'fromTypeArg != null' clause with the comment that parameters must be absent from the subject type, within the wildcard bounds, or an exact match. I verified with a clean rebuild that removing that clause makes testIsAssignable fail; it passes on the variant.
notes: Reference check: re-inserting the gold's null skip passes the trigger, the ownership tests and the full suite with no failures. Bypasses recorded: (1) hop 4 ToStringStyle.assignableUnder: replace 'return StringUtils.conformsTo(type, (ParameterizedType) toType, typeVarAssigns);' with 'return TypeUtils.isAssignable(type, toType, typeVarAssigns);'. (2) hop 3 StrBuilder.meetsBound: replace 'return ToStringStyle.assignableUnder(type, toType, typeVarAssigns);' with 'return org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.TypeUtils.isAssignable(type, toType, typeVarAssigns);'. Minor observations, not counted as leakage: (i) the builder added javadoc to the now-public TypeUtils.unrollVariableAssignments stating '@return ... null if it has no assignment'. It is accurate and applies to toTypeArg too, but it is a mild cue toward the null case. (ii) The lie sentence was appended after the @return tag without a leading ' * ', so it reads as a continuation of @return and is visually distinctive; this is the rewrite_facade artifact. (iii) TypeUtils.isAssignable(Type,Type,Map), getTypeArguments(Type,Class,Map) and unrollVariableAssignments were widened from private to public so the hops can call them. Harness caveat for future audits: copying a built checkout with cp -R gives sources and classes the same mtime, so ant skips recompilation after a source edit.
